\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{شرجی} (sharji)}{شرجی (sharji)}]{\fa{شرجی} (sharji) — muggy, humid (and hot)}

\label{lesson:FA-C477-sharji}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to freeze, then the Persian for to melt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{شرجی}}
\textbf{\fa{شرجی}} (\emph{sharji}) — \textquotedblleft{}muggy, humid (and hot)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{تابستان} \fa{در} \fa{بندر} \fa{هوا} \fa{شرجی} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Tâbestân dar bandar havâ sharji ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In summer the air in the port is muggy.
\end{quote}

Said of the Gulf coast in summer.

\begin{cousinweb}
The origin of \emph{sharji} is not settled, and EtymDB does not list it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sharji}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sharji}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{sharji}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to freeze, then the Persian for to melt, then say \emph{sharji} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{رطوبت} (rotubat)}{رطوبت (rotubat)}]{\fa{رطوبت} (rotubat) — humidity, damp}

\label{lesson:FA-C477-rotubat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to melt, then the Persian for muggy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{رطوبت}}
\textbf{\fa{رطوبت}} (\emph{rotubat}) — \textquotedblleft{}humidity, damp\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{رطوبت} \fa{هوا} \fa{امروز} \fa{خیلی} \fa{بالاست}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Rotubat-e havâ emruz kheyli bâlâst.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The humidity is very high today.
\end{quote}

\emph{Martub} — humid.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{rotubat} was borrowed from Arabic and is usually traced to Arabic \emph{ruṭūba} 'moisture, damp'. EtymDB does not list it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گرمازدگی} (garmâzadegi)}{گرمازدگی (garmâzadegi)}]{\fa{گرمازدگی} (garmâzadegi) — heatstroke}

\label{lesson:FA-C477-garmazadegi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for muggy, then the Persian for humidity.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گرمازدگی}}
\textbf{\fa{گرمازدگی}} (\emph{garmâzadegi}) — \textquotedblleft{}heatstroke\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{کارگر} \fa{در} \fa{آفتاب} \fa{گرمازدگی} \fa{گرفت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Kârgar dar âftâb garmâzadegi gereft.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The worker got heatstroke in the sun.
\end{quote}

\emph{garmâ} 'heat' + \emph{zade} 'struck' + \emph{-gi}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{garmâzadegi} is a native compound of \emph{garmâ} 'heat', from \emph{garm} 'warm', \emph{zade} 'struck', from \emph{zadan} 'to strike', and the noun ending \emph{-gi}: being struck by the heat.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for muggy, then the Persian for humidity, then say \emph{garmâzadegi} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{معتدل} (mo'tadel)}{معتدل (mo'tadel)}]{\fa{معتدل} (mo'tadel) — mild, temperate}

\label{lesson:FA-C477-motadel}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for humidity, then the Persian for heatstroke.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{معتدل}}
\textbf{\fa{معتدل}} (\emph{mo'tadel}) — \textquotedblleft{}mild, temperate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{هوای} \fa{بهار} \fa{در} \fa{این} \fa{شهر} \fa{معتدل} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Havâ-ye bahâr dar in shahr mo'tadel ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The spring weather in this town is mild.
\end{quote}

Also of people: moderate.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{mo'tadel} was borrowed from Arabic and is usually traced to Arabic \emph{muʿtadil} 'balanced, moderate'. EtymDB does not list it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آفتاب} \fa{گرفتن} (âftâb gereftan)}{آفتاب گرفتن (âftâb gereftan)}]{\fa{آفتاب} \fa{گرفتن} (âftâb gereftan) — to sunbathe}

\label{lesson:FA-C477-aftab-gereftan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for heatstroke, then the Persian for mild.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آفتاب} \fa{گرفتن}}
\textbf{\fa{آفتاب} \fa{گرفتن}} (\emph{âftâb gereftan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to sunbathe\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{گردشگرها} \fa{کنار} \fa{دریا} \fa{آفتاب} \fa{میگرفتند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Gardeshgar-hâ kenâr-e daryâ âftâb migereftand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The tourists were sunbathing by the sea.
\end{quote}

\emph{âftâb} 'sun' + \emph{gereftan} 'to take'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{âftâb gereftan} is built from \emph{âftâb} 'sunshine', which EtymDB traces to Middle Persian, and the native verb \emph{gereftan} 'to take'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
